statement: Monday sets the weekly high less often than a random walk would.
metric: Share of complete Monday–Friday weeks whose high forms on Monday, minus the within-week permutation baseline (percentage points).
criterion: Estimate below zero over the evaluation window.
basis: Discovery on SPY daily bars 2006–2025: −4.3 pp, grade A.

statement: A limit order at the prior month's low does not beat buying at the first session's open of the month.
metric: Mean per-purchase price improvement versus first-session open (%).
criterion: Estimate at or below zero over the evaluation window.
basis: Discovery on SPY daily bars 2006–2025: −0.34% per purchase, grade D; limit filled in 33% of months.

statement: Prior-week levels add less than two percentage points beyond geometry to the chance of reaching the high side first within ten sessions.
metric: Upper-first rate of events minus geometry-matched controls (percentage points).
criterion: Absolute estimate below 2 pp over the evaluation window.
basis: Discovery on SPY daily bars 2006–2025: +0.9 pp, grade C.

statement: The 15:00 UTC hour returns more than the average hour of the day.
metric: Mean log return of the 15:00 UTC hour minus the mean of all hours (basis points).
criterion: Estimate above zero over the evaluation window.
basis: Published research on Bitcoin intraday seasonality; not examined on this project's data before registration.

statement: Overnight returns exceed intraday returns on average.
metric: Mean overnight log return (prior close to open) minus mean intraday log return (open to close), basis points.
criterion: Estimate above zero over the evaluation window.
basis: Academic literature on overnight versus intraday returns; SPY 2006–2025 overnight mean +2.0 bps, grade C.

statement: Closed weeks' lows are traded again within 10 sessions more often than arbitrary levels at the same volatility-scaled distance.
metric: Share of closed weeks whose low is traded again within 10 sessions minus the control share (time-to-revisit study), percentage points.
criterion: Estimate above zero for weeks closing in the evaluation window.
basis: Author's thesis of 2026-10-30 that prior-period levels attract price; registered before any real-data result of the study was seen.

statement: In weeks that have traded above the prior week's high but not below its low by the close of the week's third session, a long held from that close to the week's last close returns more, on average, than across all weeks at the same point.
metric: Average change from the third session's close to the week's last close, in ATR at the start of the week, in qualifying weeks minus all weeks at the same point (trade plan from here, long to the period's end).
criterion: Estimate above zero over the weeks of the evaluation window.
basis: Money-terms result of the report of 2026-11-05 (SPY week after three sessions, prior week's high traded and low not: ended the week above that close in 63.8% of 287 past weeks against 58.2% of all 562, grade A), seen before registration; to be evaluated only on weeks after registration (specification 0005).

statement: In the same weeks, fewer reach 1 ATR below the third session's close before the week ends than across all weeks at the same point.
metric: Share of qualifying weeks that trade 1 ATR (at the start of the week) below the third session's close before the week's last close, minus the share for all weeks at the same point, percentage points.
criterion: Estimate below zero over the weeks of the evaluation window.
basis: Money-terms result of the report of 2026-11-05 (SPY week after three sessions, prior week's high traded and low not: 21.3% of past weeks reached 1 ATR below against 29.4% of all weeks, grade A), seen before registration; to be evaluated only on weeks after registration (specification 0005).

statement: Weeks that start in SPY's most volatile third (starting ATR at or above the 67th percentile of all earlier sessions) return more, from the third session's close to the week's last close, than all weeks at the same point.
metric: Average change from the third session's close to the week's last close, in ATR at the start of the week, in volatile-start weeks minus all weeks (trade plans by volatility regime, long held).
criterion: Estimate above zero over the weeks of the evaluation window.
basis: Author's thesis that equity returns are higher after volatile periods (risk premium and rebounds); registered before any real-data result of the regime study (specification 0007) was seen.

statement: In weeks that start in Bitcoin's calmest third (starting ATR below the 33rd percentile of all earlier days), a long held from the third day's close to the week's last close returns no more than in all weeks at the same point.
metric: Average change from the third day's close to the week's last close, in ATR at the start of the week, in calm-start weeks minus all weeks.
criterion: Estimate at or below zero over the weeks of the evaluation window.
basis: Control hypothesis: no directional effect of a calm start is expected in crypto; registered before any real-data result of the regime study was seen.

statement: Over the NDX history from 1986, the share of months whose lowest close falls in the first five sessions is within 3 percentage points of the share obtained when each month's own daily returns are shuffled: no timing effect beyond drift, volatility and the arcsine law.
metric: Item 'First week' of card NDX.extremes.month_low: observed share minus shuffled share, in percentage points (specification 0008).
criterion: Estimate between -3 and +3 percentage points and grade C or weaker in the first report that includes specification 0008.
basis: Founder's thesis that the month's low can be anticipated (power of three); the expected answer was written before the study ran on real data. Criteria: the recommended options of specification 0008 (shuffle control, closing prices, five-session windows), taken when the founder asked to continue on 2026-11-06.

statement: Bitcoin's month high forms in the last seven days of the month less often than when each month's own daily returns are shuffled.
metric: Item 'Last week' of card BTC-USD.extremes.month_high computed on the complete months of the evaluation window only: observed share minus shuffled share, in percentage points (specification 0008).
criterion: Estimate below zero over the 24 months of the evaluation window.
basis: Found in-sample on 2026-11-06 (25.7% against 38.9%, grade B, 109 months; RESULTS_2026-11-06_EXTREMES). Registered for evaluation on later months only; 24 months give little power, so a failure to confirm is not a refutation.

statement: Ether's month low forms in the last seven days of the month less often than when each month's own daily returns are shuffled.
metric: Item 'Last week' of card ETH-USD.extremes.month_low computed on the complete months of the evaluation window only: observed share minus shuffled share, in percentage points (specification 0008).
criterion: Estimate below zero over the 24 months of the evaluation window.
basis: Found in-sample on 2026-11-06 (21.2% against 30.5%, grade B, 104 months; RESULTS_2026-11-06_EXTREMES). Registered for evaluation on later months only; 24 months give little power, so a failure to confirm is not a refutation.

statement: When SPY's Monday low is still untested at the close of Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday, it is traded again before the week ends about as often as an equally distant arbitrary level: the real level adds little beyond distance.
metric: Item 'Before the week ends' of card SPY.recent_lows.monday: observed share minus the distance control, in percentage points (specification 0010).
criterion: Estimate between -5 and +5 percentage points and grade C or weaker in the first report that includes specification 0010.
basis: Founder's thesis that a market rising without touching its lows comes back at least to Monday's low; the expected answer was written before the study ran on real data. Criteria: the recommended options of specification 0010, taken when the founder asked to continue on 2026-11-06.

statement: In Bitcoin and Ether, a Monday low still untested later in the week is traded again before the week ends less often than an equally distant arbitrary level.
metric: Item 'Before the week ends' of cards BTC-USD.recent_lows.monday and ETH-USD.recent_lows.monday computed on the weeks of the evaluation window only: observed share minus the distance control, in percentage points (specification 0010), pooled over both coins.
criterion: Pooled estimate below zero over the evaluation window.
basis: Found in-sample on 2026-11-06 (Bitcoin 20.4% against 25.4%, grade A; Ether 22.7% against 27.8%, grade B; RESULTS_2026-11-06_RECENT_LOWS). Registered for evaluation on later weeks only.
